sections.notes: Use a split layout because the product supports a media-rich hero. Left: headline, subheadline, supporting line, primary CTA. sections.notes: Make logos the dominant trust signal. Use a horizontal row of recognizable partner/customer logos as placeholders only if actual logos are unavailable in source content. Emphasize image generation, editing, composition, text rendering, output quality, and structural fidelity.

sections.variantHint: feature-led editorial section with narrative cards and capability list
sections.notes: Present Seedance 1.5 Pro as the second standalone module. Use headline, description, optional CTA if provided, then readable cards or list blocks for capabilities. Keep the storytelling focused on text-to-video, audio-visual synchronization, multilingual lip-sync, and cinematic control. Maintain dark-theme consistency and avoid overly cramped card layouts.

sections.variantHint: multi-column footer with product links, company links, and support
sections.notes: Include a standard enterprise footer. Keep it compact, dark, and utility-focused with legal/support/navigation links. No extra promotional section.

figmaExecutionNotes: Use a dark theme across the entire page; ensure all section frames are built with consistent dark tokens and high-contrast text.
Prioritize logo-based trust above testimonials; do not add testimonial, pricing, or form sections because the input does not support them.
Keep feature sections readable and avoid grid-inside-grid structures; use editorial cards or staggered stacks instead.
Use human-face MP4/video treatment in the hero if the media asset is available; do not replace motion with a static image.
Maintain a fixed top strip in the desktop and mobile frame specs.
Design the gallery as a creative media showcase with mixed video and image tiles, not a generic photo grid.
Mobile should stack sections in the same order, with single-column feature layouts and a full-width CTA strip.
Do not invent unsupported sections such as testimonials, pricing, forms, or news.

heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 for image creation and Seedance 1.5 Pro for video generation—built for professional visual content at enterprise quality.
heroStrategy.designNote: Hero should feel premium and media-rich, but not generic: use a full-bleed warm light mesh gradient with precision-line overlays, then layer an abstract product mockup stack slightly off-center for an unexpected composition. Keep the headline and CTA anchored in a left content rail while the right/center zone carries a polished mockup trio: one image-generation frame, one video preview card with autoplay-like motion implied through a static frame sequence, and one capability chip cluster. No human faces; use UI shells, generated asset previews, and a logo trust band beneath the fold. Accent buttons and chips must use the brand brown-orange. Add subtle grain, soft shadows, and a fade-up/stagger entrance to preserve enterprise polish.

repetitionBreakers: Hero uses a split media-first composition.
How-it-works uses a numbered 3-step horizontal sequence.
Proof uses a static logo grid for trust.
Features shift to alternating editorial panels for image vs video.
Final CTA becomes a centered conversion block with a strong visual anchor.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro by ByteDance
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 for AI image generation and Seedance 1.5 Pro for AI video generation—enterprise-ready tools for high-quality visual content creation.

sections.backgroundTreatment: soft light gradient with precision-line accents and a premium media panel
sections.designNote: Make the headline answer what this is: enterprise AI image and video generation by ByteDance. Keep the subheadline specific to creative, marketing, design, and video teams. Use the CTA text exactly as 'Get started' in a solid accent button. Add a compact 3-point benefit stack beneath the CTA and place a polished product mockup on the right showing both image and video outputs. This is the loudest section and should carry the ad continuity.

Use 3 to 6 recognisable enterprise/client logos in a clean flex-wrap grid. Keep it prominent and close to the hero because trustStrategy is logos-first. If true logos are unavailable, substitute a compact metric strip, but prefer logos. This section should feel quiet, efficient, and immediately credible.

Insert the required warm-traffic step section here: 3 steps, under 60 seconds. Use a numbered horizontal sequence with very short copy: 1) Describe your prompt or upload a source, 2) Generate image or video output, 3) Refine and export for production. Keep the visual treatment different from the logo strip by using larger step cards with a timeline line or arrows. Make CTA buttons within the section read exactly 'Get started' if included. This section should reduce friction fast.

Reinforce proof with a compact, industry-specific credibility band. Since logos already lead, keep this section lighter: a short headline plus optional logo cluster or supporting outcome statements. If adding support copy, focus on enterprise-ready visual production speed, multimodal precision, and creative control. Avoid a generic testimonial wall here so the page rhythm stays sharp.

Because there are 5+ features, do not use a flat static grid. Use tabs with a preview panel for Seedream 4.5, then alternate the next block for Seedance 1.5 Pro. Seedream should spotlight text-to-image, multimodal editing, multi-image composition, and typographic rendering. Seedance should spotlight text-to-video, audio-visual sync, multilingual lip-sync, and cinematic camera control. Keep adjacent blocks visually different: one side-first preview layout, one text-first editorial panel. Use strong visual contrast, with one section on white and the next on a tinted surface.

Present two purchase paths as centered enterprise quote cards rather than a dense comparison table. Keep the Seedance pricing visible since it has a listed starting price, and keep Seedream as request-a-quote. Use one highlighted card and one secondary card. CTA buttons, if present, must be exactly 'Get started' to obey the single CTA rule, though pricing copy can still mention quote/request context in body text.

Use a 3-card grid because there are 4+ testimonials available. Select the strongest quotes from creative director, video producer, and art director voices to match the audience. Keep cards concise and believable, with role-first attribution. Avoid carousel motion unless necessary; a static grid feels more premium and less salesy here.

Close with a centered lead-capture card that feels like a premium decision point. The headline should be action-oriented and the CTA button must be exactly 'Get started'. Keep the form minimal. This is the conversion endpoint, so make it visually distinct from the testimonial section by using a stronger card elevation, tighter spacing, and a clearer CTA block.

blueprint.designPersonality: An editorial enterprise AI page with premium warmth, sharp hierarchy, and media-rich proof. It should feel trustworthy for business buyers, but visually exciting enough for creative teams—structured, elegant, and conversion-focused with logos front and center.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a strong media-first presentation with a hero product mockup, a creative gallery containing both video and image examples, floating capability chips, and a logo trust band. Avoid human faces in the hero. Use abstract UI shells, model preview frames, and polished media cards rather than cropped promotional imagery.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Full-width top banner with brand/logo anchor, oversized H1, short supporting paragraph, and a compact benefit list with icon bullets; stacked content on a single strong visual band rather than a split media hero.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Hero band followed by a lead-capture/form block, then feature sections in a linear vertical flow; uses clear module separation and repeated top-aligned headings with concise body copy.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Primarily simple rectangular content cards/panels with light borders or subtle elevation; minimal decoration, emphasis on typography and list structure over imagery-heavy cards.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA is prominent and action-oriented in the hero; secondary CTAs appear as section-level request/demo actions. CTA treatment is likely button-based with strong contrast and repeated at key decision points.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing pattern evident; likely absent in favor of lead-generation and inquiry-based conversion.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in the provided reference; infer a standard low-information utility footer if present.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Low-media density landing page; brand logo in hero and likely no dominant illustrative hero image. Visual communication relies more on typography, icon bullets, and structured form content than on large media panels.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Single product-intro blocks per feature family with label chips, headline, descriptive paragraph, then a bullet/list of capabilities; progressive disclosure through stacked feature groups rather than tabs or accordions.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form block immediately after hero, presented as a card/panel with a clear heading and multiple hidden tracking fields; form is a primary conversion surface rather than a small inline embed.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, utility-driven presentation with no obvious motion system; interaction emphasis appears to be on form submission and section navigation rather than animated storytelling.

Use icon bullets and short lists to communicate capabilities quickly.
Maintain generous spacing and clear section separation for enterprise credibility.
Avoid carousel/tab dependence; the reference reads as a straightforward static landing page.
If adding visuals, keep them secondary to copy and form entry points.

designStrategy.reasoning: This is a high-intent enterprise-style category page for two advanced AI products, so the page should drive demo/quote capture rather than broad awareness. Because the visitor trusts logos most, the first credibility layer should be a prominent logo band, supported by concise proof and testimonials later. The ideal narrative is product-led: show what Seedream and Seedance do, then prove quality through a media gallery, feature depth, and customer quotes. A dark, premium, immersive treatment fits the AI/video category and helps the hero feel cinematic, but the layout must stay readable and conversion-focused. The hero should be message-dominant with a professional human face element, while the rest of the page should flow vertically with clear section separation, repeated CTAs, and a visible form to reduce friction.
